title: Cascade Prefill Coordinator and Kernel Slate Scheduler
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
BACKGROUND: We see intermittent tail spikes in decode latency for mixed-tenancy workloads with heterogeneous sequence lengths. Existing admission logic admits batches mostly by arrival time and simple slot reservation; kernel selection is reactive and sometimes runs suboptimal kernels for attention-heavy batches.

GOAL: Reduce p95/p99 decode tail latency by introducing a Cascade Prefill Coordinator (CPC) that applies lightweight, telemetry-driven admission tiers and a Kernel Slate Scheduler (KSS) that proactively selects a small set of compatible kernels for each candidate batch prior to decode. The CPC aims to avoid long-prefill queuing for short sequences and opportunistically cascade requests to higher-capacity lanes when safe. The KSS leverages attention-profile fingerprints to prefer kernels with pre-warmed attention kernels/kv layouts.

SCOPE: Produce a staged implementation running in the host inference runtime, instrumented to allow A/B on canary pools: (1) CPC admission tiers (fast-path, pooled-prefill, cascade-to-bulk), (2) per-batch kernel slate generation and scoring, (3) telemetry hooks and cost accounting, (4) observable dashboards and gating for rollback.

DESIGN HIGHLIGHTS: 
- Cascade Prefill Coordinator: classifies incoming prefill requests into three fast admission bands using a small stateful estimator (recent sequence length distribution, tenant priority, and current slot occupancy). Fast-path admits sub-32-token prefill to low-latency slots; medium-path collects small batches until a size threshold or timeout; bulk-path aggregates or routes to pooled GPUs with optimized kernels. Uses TTL-based fingerprints to avoid starvation.
- Kernel Slate Scheduler: before decode, KSS constructs a slate of 2-3 candidate kernels (e.g., attention-optimized kernel variants, fused KV-layout kernels) and scores them by estimated latency and expected memory impact. The scheduler uses a microcost model trained from recent kernel telemetry (latency per seq_len, kv-hit rate) and selects the kernel with the best trade-off for the target latency SLO.
- Telemetry & Feedback: per-request labels include admission-band, chosen-slate, score metrics, actual decode latency, and kernel hotness. CPC adjusts thresholds every 30s in response to p95 drift using PID-like smoothing.

ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: 
- p95 decode latency improvement of at least 20% and p99 improvement of 10–25% on mixed workloads in canary pools compared to baseline.
- No regression in 99th-percentile throughput for reserved capacity customers.
- Observable metrics/backfills available in Console; ability to toggle CPC/KSS per-pool.
- Rollback route verified and tested.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN: 
1) Implementation spike (perf harness) to implement CPC classifier and KSS prototype (unit tests + microbench).
2) Integrate telemetry tags and dashboards (Console).
3) Canary rollout to internal dev clusters with synthetic traffic and production trace replay.
4) Gradual ramp to small customer-tenants, monitor cost/latency and rollback if negative.

TRADEOFFS & RISKS: 
- Better tail latency may increase GPU utilization in burst windows; must ensure cost per token targets still met.
- Kernel slate scoring adds small compute cost prior to decode; measuring and bounding that overhead is critical.
- Complexity increases control surface and more knobs—need good defaults and safe fallback to existing admission.

METRICS & SUCCESS SIGNALS: 
- Baseline: p50/p95/p99 decode latency, tokens/sec, pref fill queue length distribution, kernel cold-start counts.
- Targets: p95 down 20%+, p99 down 10%+, token-cost delta <+5% in steady state.

ROLLOUT & SAFETY: 
- Feature flags: per-cluster and per-tenant flags. Canary group 5% of production traffic for 48h, then 25% for 72h, then 100% of dedicated pools for non-sensitive tenants.
- Automated rollback on: p99 latency > baseline + 10% for 30m or error-rate increase > 0.5%.

DOCUMENTS/ARTIFACTS: See artifacts field for design doc, perf results, and PR.

NOTES: This ticket intentionally keeps kernel slate size small (2–3) to limit pre-decode cost and to allow fast evaluation. If CPC indicates heavy tail pressure, KSS will prefer conservative kernels to reduce preemption within GPUs.
acceptance_criteria: p95 decode latency <= baseline * 0.8 in canary; p99 <= baseline * 0.9 to 0.95; throughput regressions <= 1% for reserved capacity; telemetry visible in Console and flag toggle validated.
comments: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting — agreed to prototype CPC as classifier + short-lived counters. Action: Marco to spike KSS microcost model. (Aisha, Marco, Lin)

2026-02-28: Design review — PM (Claire) requested explicit rollback SLOs and customer-impact labeling. Added customer_impact=medium. Design doc updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Cascade+Prefill+Coordinator+Design
2026-03-03: Implementation — initial CPC + slate prototype merged behind feature flag in runtime repo. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1876. Perf team to run 48h replay.

2026-03-06: Perf run 24h replay — p95 decode improved 22% for mixed web-search traces, p99 improved 12%. Noted a small throughput dip (0.8%) on heavy-batch synthetic. Action: tune medium-path timeout and slate scoring weight.
2026-03-09: Code review feedback — add more defensive checks for kernel selection fallback (Marco). Add instrumentation for per-slate eviction counters (Lin).
2026-03-10: Testing — Canary flag enabled on dev-canary pool. Monitoring dashboards added. Next step: enable internal canary for 48h and collect cost signals.
